The binding problem is the local seeds-0-2 gate. A new mechanism node (regression to the mean) explains why all seven children of E069 lost: the tip was chosen on a lucky draw, so any change that re-draws seeds 0-2 loses ~0.25 pp in expectation. That leaves a usable budget of only ~0.04 pp, so the tree now favours margin recovery and time cuts that leave the math unchanged.\n- **Polar Express gain downgraded.** H1.2.7 moves from supported to inconclusive (0.30). The 13-seed mean (~0.7534) erases most of the +0.24 pp seen on seeds 0-2, and the MUD paper finds no gain from stronger whitening on CIFAR-10.\n- **H4.1.1 downgraded.** Its determinism evidence predates the autotune settings, so it is now inconclusive.\n- **Refuted, matching the recorded verdicts:** H1.2.4 (E075), H6.3/H6.3.1, H6.4/H6.4.1 (E070; the 'cheap marginal epoch' and asymmetric-knee story is dropped in favour of a steep ~1.1-1.4 pp/epoch slope), H7.1/H7.1.1, H7.2/H7.2.1, H7.3/H7.3.1, H1.11/H1.11.1, H1.7.4.\n- **Marked supported, with their levers exhausted:** H6, H7 and H1.7.\n- **Retired:** H1.4/H1.4.1, H1.5.2, H2.4.5 (Turbo-Muon saves only 0.8% end to end) and H4.1.5.\n- **Systems nodes revised from the search:**\n  - Gram NS saves ~29% of NS FLOPs, not ~45%, and its gate now checks the singular-value spectrum.\n  - H1.6.6 now covers per-group lr multipliers too. It was lowered to 0.40 because Dynamo guards Python floats, so compile caching is an unlikely cause.\n  - H2.5.1 moves to E069 and must log host load.\n\n**New nodes**\n- N1: official safety holds.\n- N2: regression to the mean, with N2a re-scoring E070-E076 against the 13-seed mean.\n- N3: rerun E069 unchanged to test determinism.\n- N4: Muon lr 0.20 on the Polar Express base.\n- N5: paired E069-vs-E058 comparison on seeds 3-12.\n- N6/N6a: matched-FLOP width reallocation between blocks 1 and 2.\n\nThree Lvl1 hypotheses stay open: H1, H2 and H4.\n\n**Suggested order (all except the first are offline or cheap)**\n1. Record the existing extra-seed numbers (H4.1.2, N5).\n2. RNG-shift controls on both E058 and E069 (H4.1.6).\n3. The H1.6.6 no-op check.\n4. Then math-preserving cuts (Gram NS, projection frequency, the autotune check) and margin recovery (Muon lr 0.20, averaging ramp and sync interval)."}

updates.statement: Accuracy per step is set by the structure of the update, and on this base the update geometry looks saturated. Only two levers clearly moved the mean: Muon on the conv filters (+1.3 pp on every seed, E014) and lookahead (~0.9-1 pp, E008/E020). The Polar Express gain (E069, +0.24 pp on seeds 0-2) is doubtful: E069's 13-seed mean is ~0.7534, about 0.27 pp below its seeds-0-2 score. Weaker whitening (E065 -1.51), Muon-C (E030 -1.2), NorMuon (E066 -0.26), a Muon head (E059 -0.61), batch-size schedules (E053, E055), the SGD-group lr axes (E039, E056, E072), Muon lr below 0.16 (E075 -0.89) and target smoothing (E004, E036, E068) all failed to help. Because the local gate gives a budget of only ~0.04 pp (H4), the remaining directions are margin recovery that is neutral or better in expectation: (a) the H1.6.6 no-op check, which the head/BN/lookahead closures rest on; (b) the averaging setup (H1.6.1); (c) Muon lr 0.20 on the PE base; (d) matched-FLOP width reallocation between blocks 1 and 2.
updates.reason: Rolled up the E068-E075 refutations and the review's finding that the PE gain is mostly a seeds-0-2 draw (13-seed ~0.7534). Removed OLS and stronger whitening from the 'left' list, since both were tested, and added the margin-recovery directions the review named.

updates.statement: Muon on the 4D conv filters cuts the epochs needed on CIFAR-100 by ~2.5 (9 SGD epochs -> ~6.5-6.75 Muon epochs). The working form is flattened [out, in*k*k] orthogonalized Nesterov momentum, NS3 at Frobenius scale 1, and weight-norm projection. Nesterov SGD runs the BN biases, the whitening bias and the head, and lookahead is kept. The Muon lr has cliffs on both sides: 0.36 costs ~1 pp (E019) and 0.12 on the PE base costs ~0.9 pp on every seed (E075). The 0.16-0.24 plateau was measured with plain NS3 coefficients, and 0.20 is untested on PE. Momentum 0.6-0.8 is flat. Whitening strength is first-order downward (E065 -1.51, consistent with MUD on CIFAR-10 airbench). Upward (PE coefficients, E069) the gain is uncertain: +0.24 pp on seeds 0-2 against a 13-seed mean of ~0.7534, and MUD reports NS5 == NS3. Frequency-split (E030), per-row normalization (E066) and bs 2048 (E055) all lost.
updates.reason: Added E069 with the 13-seed caveat, E075's lower lr cliff, and the MUD paper's external support for 'weaker hurts, stronger ~0'.

updates.statement: Muon lr below the tested range. On the PE tip (E069), lowering the Muon lr from 0.16 to 0.12 (0.12 was run, not the originally specified 0.11) with nothing else changed moves mean accuracy by no more than +-0.2 pp.
updates.reason: E075: -0.89 pp, with every seed lower by 0.7-1.0 pp. Even against E069's 13-seed mean (~0.7534) the loss is ~-0.6 pp, far beyond re-draw noise. The statement now names the lr value actually run.

updates.statement: Stronger whitening than NS3 (3 iterations with Polar Express coefficients from optimal_composition(num_iters=3), output rescaled to NS3's Frobenius norm) gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy on the tip at <=1% more time. The seeds-0-2 result (E069 +0.24 pp) is not confirmed on extra seeds: the 13-seed mean is ~0.7534, and MUD reports no gain from stronger orthogonalization on CIFAR-10 airbench. The decisive test is the paired E069-vs-E058 comparison on seeds 3-12.
updates.reason: Downgraded from supported. The only support is one 3-seed run whose gain matches the expected re-draw size (~0.2 pp unpaired, per Jordan's variance formula), and the 13-seed mean falls ~0.27 pp below seeds 0-2. All seven E069 children lost, which fits an optimistic baseline. External evidence (MUD) also gives ~0 for stronger whitening.
This cut spends accuracy, and the local budget is ~0.04 pp (H4 regression-to-mean). bs 2048 cost 0.45 pp (E055), and E070 shows late steps are not cheap to remove. Priority lowered.

Search: the only published hard-example win (airbench96_faster) is at 45 epochs and 96%. At 6.75 epochs the early phase is step-starved (E053), and accuracy-spending cuts cannot fit the current margin.
Retired with its parent; the prior is too low for this horizon (airbench96_faster gains appear only at 45 epochs).

Cutting epochs to pay for width is now a bad trade. E070 showed -0.25 epoch costs ~0.4-0.6 pp, and E029 priced block-3 width at 0.062 pp per 1%. Superseded by the matched-FLOP block-1/2 width reallocation node.

updates.statement: With lookahead heavily weighting late iterates, the end of training matters through what it feeds the average. A non-zero tail lr supplies diverse iterates: decay-to-0 hurt (E025 -0.51 pp), a 0.15x floor was not better (E033 -0.17), and BN recalibration adds nothing (E035). The averaging setup itself (decay, sync interval, ramp exponent, EMA on top) is effectively untested. Averaging is worth ~1 pp (E008, E020), and its one tuning run (E028) matched its parent to 0.003 pp. This is the cheapest margin-recovery axis (<1% time).
updates.reason: Reframed as margin recovery under the H4 budget. No new evidence.

updates.statement: On E069, after the H1.6.6 check, a stronger or denser averaging setup gives >=+0.15 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Judge it against E069's 13-seed mean, ideally also run offline on seeds 3-12. Candidates in priority order: (t/T)^2 instead of (t/T)^3 ramp; lookahead sync every 3 steps instead of 5; an EMA over the last ~30% of steps on top of lookahead.
updates.reason: Moved to the current base and judged against the 13-seed baseline, per the review.

updates.statement: Some hyperparameter edits did not take effect in the timed path, through a code-path bug rather than compile caching. Dynamo guards Python floats on their exact value, so a changed constant recompiles rather than being silently ignored. Check offline in drafts/ on E069: (1) log the per-sync lookahead alpha actually applied; (2) log the effective per-step lr of each SGD sub-group (head, BN biases, whitening bias) and the Muon lr; (3) compare seed-0 final-weight hashes for E027 vs E028 and E047 vs E049. Supported if any pair is bit-identical or a logged value ignores its edit. In that case reopen the affected axes: lookahead first, then head/BN lr (E039/E045/E056/E072 would then have been wd-only changes).
updates.reason: Search: Dynamo float guards make a compile-cache no-op unlikely, so confidence was lowered from 0.60. Scope widened to per-group lr multipliers, because the head-lr and BN-lr closures depend on them too (review).

updates.statement: The SGD-group lrs are at their optimum: head x2 (x0.5 -0.41 pp E039; x3 ~= x2 E049) and BN-bias x64 (x128 -0.49 pp E056; x32 -0.13 pp E072, within noise). The axis is closed. Caveat: this rests on the lr multipliers actually being applied in the compiled path (H1.6.6).
updates.reason: E072 completed the last untested setting. All directions are flat or worse, so the axis is closed, conditional on H1.6.6.
E072: -0.13 pp against the predicted >=+0.2. The outcome is 0.33 pp from the prediction, so it is not a near miss even against the inflated E069 baseline.
The prediction was neutrality, and E052 gave +0.04 pp, within the paired noise band. One result, but it supports a neutral claim, and nothing contradicts it.

updates.statement: How strongly Muon orthogonalizes should be scheduled over training, with weaker, less whitened updates late. E065 refuted the RMS-matched form (-1.51 pp). Search shows Hiverge's actual schedule (Frobenius 0.50->0.08 before NS3) is not RMS-matched. It shrinks the update size and comes paired with lr 0.205, intermittent projection and Muon weight decay, so E065 tested a different mechanism from Hiverge's. Either way, less whitening at matched update size hurts on this base.
updates.reason: Added the search finding that E065 did not replicate Hiverge's actual mechanism. The refutation stands for the RMS-matched form.
E068: online label smoothing -0.24 pp against a predicted +0.25. With E004 and E036, every target-smoothing variant is flat to negative at this horizon.
E068 scored -0.24 pp against a predicted >=+0.25 pp. The 0.49 pp gap between prediction and outcome is well beyond paired noise.

updates.statement: With the recipe held fixed, per-step GPU work can still be cut by a few percent at unchanged accuracy, but only by removing GPU work: launch overhead is hidden (E005, E038). Under the H4 budget (~0.04 pp), math-preserving cuts are the only safe time lever. Systems total so far is ~11% (E007, E010, E021, E023, E034), plus the curriculum (H2.3) and the block-1 freeze (E058 -4.7%). Candidates left: (1) re-profile E069 first; the last profiles are from E003/E016 and predate the curriculum, freeze and PE. (2) Gram NS: stable form ~-29% NS FLOPs at aspect ratio 9; needs fp16 and a restart, and squares the condition number. (3) Projection frequency (H2.4.3). (4) max-autotune for the 300 W PCIe judge (H2.5.1). Turbo-Muon and NS2 variants have <1% published upside.
updates.reason: Search revised the Gram NS saving (-29%, not -45%) and the Turbo-Muon saving (-0.8% end to end). The review stresses that only math-preserving cuts fit the margin and that the tip has not been profiled since E016.

updates.statement: Non-conv or redundant work that takes a visible share of GPU time can be cut at no accuracy cost by doing less of it. Instances: the atomic pool backward (E010 -2.0%), SiLU (E021 -2.2%), a batched compiled Muon step (E023 -2.7%), freezing the whitening bias after epoch 1 (E034 -3.0%), and freezing block 1 for the last 20% (E058 -4.7%). Further freezing gives too little: block-2 first conv -0.9% (E071), eval-mode BN in frozen block 1 -0.2% (E076). The remaining Muon cost (~1.4 ms/step, ~6% of the run) is GPU kernel time (E038). Candidates are Gram NS (stable ~-29% NS FLOPs) and projection frequency. Fewer NS iterations risk E065-style under-whitening.
updates.reason: Added E071/E076 and the search-corrected Gram NS saving.
Search: Turbo-Muon/AOL saved only 0.8% end to end on the heavily optimized CIFAR-10 speedrun, below this node's >=1.2% bar. Fewer NS iterations also risk under-whitening (E065).
Lowered. Published NS-reduction gains in CNN speedruns are <1% (Turbo-Muon), and NS2 risks E065-style under-whitening.

updates.statement: FreezeOut-style: freezing block 1 (conv weights and BN biases) for the last ~20% of samples, through a compiled variant that detaches block 1's output plus a Muon variant without its group, cuts mean time by >=3% with accuracy within -0.2 pp (E058: -4.7%, -0.09 pp). An earlier freeze at 0.7 costs ~0.11 pp paired over 13 seeds on E058 (E061/E073). That is real but small, and it cannot fit the local gate's ~0.04 pp budget. Annealing before the freeze adds nothing (E067). The block-2 cascade (E062 -0.49) and mid-run thinning (E064 -0.54) are worse. The freeze point is settled at 0.8.
updates.reason: E073 and the 13-seed paired estimate resolved the 0.7 point. Its cost is small but too large for the current budget, so the freeze point is settled at 0.8.

updates.statement: Replace the tip's batched PE-NS3 with stabilized Gram Newton-Schulz: iterate on the out x out Gram matrix in fp16 with one restart after iteration 2, using the same PE coefficients and a 1.05 safety factor. Expected NS FLOPs -29% (60n^3 vs 84n^3 at aspect ratio 9, T=3). Gate in drafts/: (a) a profile of E069 shows NS bmm is >=50% of the Muon step; (b) on real momentum matrices, the fraction of singular values >0.5 matches PE-NS3 within 1 point and the max deviation is <1e-2; (c) debug_nan passes under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. Prediction: Muon GPU time -0.2 ms/step, mean time -0.8 to -1.2%, accuracy within +-0.15 pp of E069's 13-seed mean.
updates.reason: Search: the stable form saves ~29%, not ~45%. It needs fp16 and a restart, and it squares the condition number, which hits the small singular directions that E065 shows matter. The gate now checks the spectrum, and confidence was lowered from 0.30.

updates.statement: After clearing the Inductor cache, run E069 and an E069 variant without cudnn.benchmark and max-autotune, 2-3 times each, interleaved, logging host load and per-trial drift. The paired mean time gap will be <1.5%, so the E007 keep was within jitter. In that case drop max-autotune to free build budget and avoid kernel choices tuned on the 400 W SXM that may not transfer to the 300 W PCIe judge.
updates.reason: Moved to the current tip. Search confirms the PCIe judge's 300 W cap, and E075 showed host contention, so the run must log load.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the LOCAL accuracy gate (3-seed mean on fixed seeds 0-2 >= 0.753), not the official one. E069's 13-seed mean (~0.7534) sits ~0.34 pp above the official 40-seed bar of 0.75, which is comfortable. But the tip was selected on a good seeds-0-2 draw (0.7561), and every change re-draws those seeds. Expected regression is ~0.25 pp, so the real budget for accuracy-spending cuts is ~0.04 pp. That explains why all seven E069 children (E070-E076) lost 0.10-0.89 pp. Noise estimates have risen (0.06 pp E057, ~0.14 E070, ~0.2 from Jordan's sqrt(err/2n) at 25% error), so deltas below ~0.3 pp on an unpaired 3-seed mean are inconclusive. Score children against 13-seed means, rebuild margin with neutral-or-better changes, and favour math-preserving time cuts.
updates.reason: Restructured per the review. The 13-seed data (I098, about E069) shows official safety, while the local gate suffers regression to the mean. Search adds a theoretical per-run sd of ~0.35 pp for CIFAR-100.

updates.statement: Noise has three parts: identical-commit nondeterminism (bit-identical in E003, but that was before cudnn.benchmark and max-autotune); paired re-draw for a change at fixed seeds (E057: ~0.06 pp on the 3-seed mean on E052); and unpaired seed sampling (Jordan's formula: ~0.35 pp per run at 25% error, ~0.2 pp on a 3-seed mean). The paired estimate looks base-dependent and has grown since E057. Identical changes cost different amounts on E058 and E069 (freeze at 0.7: -0.11 vs -0.38). The E069 base may be more sensitive, or its seeds 0-2 more favourable.
updates.reason: Integrated the search variance formula and the review's point that noise estimates keep rising and that determinism evidence predates autotune.

The E003 evidence predates cudnn.benchmark=True and max-autotune (E007), which can change algorithm choice and reduction order between processes. No unchanged rerun has been done since, so the claim is unverified for the current tip. A new rerun node was added.

updates.statement: Record the extra-seed (3-12) results that already exist. E073's note cites a 13-seed paired comparison on E058, and I098 gives E069 a 13-seed mean of ~0.7534. Prediction: E058's extra-seed mean is within 0.1 pp of E069's, i.e. the ratchet inflated both tips' seeds-0-2 scores by ~0.15-0.25 pp. Refuted if E058's extra-seed mean is <=0.7510, which would leave PE a real gain.
updates.reason: The extra-seed data apparently exists (I098, E073 note) but its numbers are not recorded in the tree. The node is rewritten to record them and to serve as the PE paired test.
A historical question (E044 vs E048) with no bearing on current decisions. Extra-seed budget is better spent on E058 vs E069 and RNG-shift controls.

updates.statement: Offline in drafts/, apply 3 RNG-shift edits (1, 2 and 3 extra dummy draws from the trial generator) on both E058 and E069. Prediction: the paired per-seed sd on E069 is >=1.5x that on E058, and E069's mean over the shifts falls >=0.15 pp below 0.7561 (regression to the mean). If both bases give <=0.1 pp per seed and no mean drop, the E070-E076 losses are real effects and their refutations stand.
updates.reason: Extended to both bases. This is the discriminating test for the review's base-dependent-noise and regression-to-the-mean explanation of the E070-E076 losses.

updates.statement: Time is set by full-resolution compute after warmup. Warmup steps tolerate low resolution (E040, E047, E048) but not fewer steps (E053). Low-res steps after the lr peak cost accuracy: each half-epoch moved from 32 to 28 px costs ~0.2 pp for ~2% (E043, E054, E074), and the final map must stay >=2x2 (E050). The epoch slope at the knee on the curriculum+freeze base is still steep, ~1.1-1.4 pp/epoch: E063 (+0.07 for +0.25) and E070 (-0.63 for -0.25) together give ~0.7 pp per 0.5 epoch, plus noise. The 'asymmetric convex knee' story is dropped. The 32 px tail (3.25 epochs) and total epochs (6.75) are at their floor.
updates.reason: E070 refutes the 'marginal epoch worth ~0.3 pp' claim, and E074 confirms the boundary cost. The review's reading (steep slope plus noise) fits both runs without an ad hoc asymmetry. The core claim is supported, and its levers are exhausted.

Two consistent results: moving the 28->32 px boundary from 3.5 to 4.0 cost ~0.2 pp for only 1.6-2.3% time (E054, and E074 against the 13-seed mean). That is ~0.1 pp per 1%, no cheaper than epochs, so 28 px does not substitute for the 32 px tail.
The time arm fails in both runs (E054 -2.3%, E074 -1.6%, both below the >=2.5% bar), and accuracy fell -0.22 and -0.48 (~-0.2 against the 13-seed mean).

E070: -0.25 epoch cost 0.63 pp, ~0.36 pp even against E069's 13-seed mean. E063's +0.07 was a noisy single point on a different base, and the combined slope (~1.4 pp/epoch) restores the steep picture.
E070 dropped 0.63 pp against the >=0.25 refutation line, and still more than 0.25 pp against the deflated 13-seed baseline.

updates.statement: Each block's late learning value runs out at a different time. Block 1 is nearly done by ~0.8 of training (E058 -0.09 pp for -4.7%; 0.7 costs ~0.11 pp paired over 13 seeds). Block 2 is still learning at 0.9 (E062 -0.49 pp), even its first conv alone (E071 -0.9% time, too small). Mid-run thinning hurts (E064), and early steps cannot be removed (E053). All the refinements tested have failed: annealing before the freeze (E067), eval-mode BN (E076, no time saved) and a partial block-2 freeze (E071). The axis is exhausted at the 0.8 block-1 freeze.
updates.reason: The core claim is supported by E058 vs E062. All three refinement Lvl2s (H7.1, H7.2, H7.3) are now refuted.
E067: annealing block 1 before the 0.7 freeze matched E061 (+0.02 pp). The cost of an earlier freeze is lost learning, not an abrupt stop.
E067 scored within 0.05 pp of E061 rather than E058, the case the prediction pre-registered as refuting.

E076: eval-mode BN in frozen block 1 saved only 0.2% (<0.7% bar), so the BN statistic work is already negligible. The -0.54 pp accuracy drop is unexplained. It is probably regression to the mean against E069's optimistic seeds 0-2 and is folded into the RNG-shift control (H4.1.6).
The time arm failed (-0.2% vs the >=0.7% predicted). The accuracy loss (-0.54 pp vs seeds 0-2) needs per-seed checking but does not rescue the hypothesis.
E071: freezing block 2's first conv for the last 10% saved only 0.9% and cost 0.10 pp. Combined with E062, late block-2 freezing is not a useful lever.
E071 missed the >=1% time bar (-0.9%; the FLOP cut is deterministic, so this is not jitter), and accuracy sat at the -0.1 pp edge.

updates.statement: A resolution curriculum of bilinearly downsampled whole images (antialiased, inside the compiled augment) cuts FLOPs at small accuracy cost while the low-res steps fall in or near warmup. Current form: 20 px for epochs 0-1.5, 28 px for 1.5-3.5, then 32 px for 3.25 epochs. Prices: 24 px warmup -3.0%/+0.08 pp (E040); 24->20 px -3.5%/-0.18 (E047); 28 px stage -5.2%/+0.02 (E048, -0.23 in E044); 28 px to 3.5 epochs -1.5%/-0.10 (E051); 28 px to 4.0 epochs -1.6 to -2.3%/~-0.2 (E054, E074, both infeasible). 16 px collapses (E050 -1.41, 1x1 final map). Fable's CIFAR-10 SOTA independently uses 24->28->32. The 32 px tail is at its floor.
updates.reason: Added E074 and the search's independent support (Fable).

new.statement: Official safety is not the risk. On 13 seeds the tip's mean (~0.7534 for E069) sits ~0.34 pp above the official 40-seed bar of 0.75. With a per-run sd of ~0.35 pp, the 40-seed mean has sd ~0.06 pp, about 5 sd of headroom. A recipe whose 13-seed mean stays >=0.752 is officially safe even if it misses the local 0.753 gate.

Regression to the mean against the local gate. Each keep was chosen partly because seeds 0-2 drew well, so any change that re-draws those seeds loses ~0.2-0.3 pp in expectation, regardless of its true effect. This is why all seven E069 children (E070-E076) lost, including near-neutral ones (E072 -0.13, E076 -0.54). It also explains why the same freeze at 0.7 cost -0.11 pp paired over 13 seeds but -0.38 on seeds 0-2 (E073). Consequences: only changes that are neutral or better in expectation can be stacked, refutations judged against the seeds-0-2 tip by margins <0.3 pp are inconclusive, and children should be scored against 13-seed means.

Re-score E070-E076 against E069's 13-seed mean (~0.7534) instead of 0.7561. Prediction: E072 (-0.13 -> ~+0.14), E071 (~+0.17) and E076 (~-0.27) fall within +-0.3 pp of the 13-seed mean, so they are re-draw-sized. E075 (-0.62) and E070 (-0.36) stay beyond it. If this holds, E073, E074 and E076 count as inconclusive on accuracy (E076 and E074 still fail on time), and E075 and E070 remain real refutations.

Rerun E069 unchanged once (same commit, fresh process, Inductor cache intact). Prediction: per-seed accuracies match within 0.02 pp. If any seed differs by more than 0.05 pp, cudnn.benchmark/max-autotune has introduced process-level nondeterminism, which adds to every delta since E007, and E003 no longer supports H4.1.1.

Muon lr upward on the PE base. On E069, raise the Muon lr from 0.16 to 0.20 with nothing else changed (0-d tensor, no recompile). PE spreads the same Frobenius norm over ~95% of singular directions instead of ~86%, so per-direction rotation is smaller and the optimum may have moved up. E075 shows 0.16 sits near a lower cliff (0.12: -0.89 pp). Prediction: >=+0.15 pp against E069's 13-seed mean, checked offline on seeds 3-12. A drop of >=0.3 pp means the plateau is narrow and 0.16 is already optimal.
new.source: review; search:arxiv 2605.13079 (Spectral Flattening Is All Muon Needs)

new.statement: Paired PE test on extra seeds. Offline on seeds 3-12, using existing runs where available, E069 (PE coefficients) minus E058 (NS3 coefficients) has a paired mean delta of >=+0.1 pp. If it is <0.1 pp, the E069 gain on seeds 0-2 was a re-draw: H1.2.7 is refuted, and the plain coefficients are kept as the cheaper-to-reason-about base.

Under Muon, the block-1/block-2 width split (128/384, inherited from SGD airbench) is not optimal. Muon uses capacity more efficiently than SGD (E037: block-1 depth is worth ~2x under Muon). Shifting width between the two blocks at matched FLOPs may raise accuracy at unchanged time. Only block-3 width and block-1 depth have been varied so far.

On E069, change block widths 128/384 -> 160/352 (multiples of 32) at matched step FLOPs (within +-1.5% time), keeping block 3 at 576 and the Muon shape groups batched. Prediction: >=+0.15 pp against E069's 13-seed mean, checked on seeds 3-12. A result within +-0.15 pp means the width split is flat. Warm up the new shapes in build() with channels_last and run debug_nan.

structured_output.summary:
The tree was behind its own evidence; this revision brings it up to date. The biggest change is that the accuracy budget is now treated as the real constraint.

**What changed**
- **H4 restructured.** Official safety is now its own node: on 13 seeds the tip is ~0.34 pp above the 40-seed bar of 0.75. The binding problem is the local seeds-0-2 gate. A new mechanism node (regression to the mean) explains why all seven children of E069 lost: the tip was chosen on a lucky draw, so any change that re-draws seeds 0-2 loses ~0.25 pp in expectation. That leaves a usable budget of only ~0.04 pp, so the tree now favours margin recovery and time cuts that leave the math unchanged.
